pages.text: During Physical Education on the school field, Mr Kotei asked the class to place one hand over their chests. “Stand still and feel your heartbeat,” he said. Adoley felt a calm, steady beat: thump, thump, thump.
sentences: During Physical Education on the school field, Mr Kotei asked the class to place one hand over their chests.
“Stand still and feel your heartbeat,” he said.
Adoley felt a calm, steady beat: thump, thump, thump.
pages.alt: On a sunny grassy Ghanaian school field, Adoley and her classmates in red-and-gold PE kit stand calmly with one hand over their chests as Mr Kotei demonstrates.

pages.text: “Now run on the spot for one full minute!” called Mr Kotei. Adoley pumped her arms and knees as briskly as she could. When the whistle blew to stop, her chest rose and fell rapidly. Her heart was thumping fast, and she was breathing hard.
sentences: “Now run on the spot for one full minute!” called Mr Kotei.
Adoley pumped her arms and knees as briskly as she could.
When the whistle blew to stop, her chest rose and fell rapidly.
Her heart was thumping fast, and she was breathing hard.
pages.alt: Adoley running energetically on the spot with knees high on the school field while Mr Kotei times the class with his whistle ready.

pages.text: “Why is my heart racing?” Adoley asked. “When you run, your leg muscles work hard and need extra oxygen,” explained Mr Kotei. “Your lungs breathe faster to take in fresh air, and your heart pumps faster to carry oxygen in your blood to those muscles.”
sentences: “Why is my heart racing?” Adoley asked.
“When you run, your leg muscles work hard and need extra oxygen,” explained Mr Kotei.
“Your lungs breathe faster to take in fresh air, and your heart pumps faster to carry oxygen in your blood to those muscles.”
pages.alt: Mr Kotei placing one hand over his chest and gesturing kindly toward his legs as he explains how lungs, heart, and muscles work together to curious Adoley.

pages.text: The class sat together in the shade of a mango tree to rest. After a few quiet minutes, Adoley checked her heartbeat again; it had slowed right down. “It is steady again,” she smiled. “Yes,” said Mr Kotei. “Your body adjusts to what you need.”
sentences: The class sat together in the shade of a mango tree to rest.
After a few quiet minutes, Adoley checked her heartbeat again; it had slowed right down.
“It is steady again,” she smiled.
“Yes,” said Mr Kotei.
“Your body adjusts to what you need.”
pages.alt: Under the cool shade of a large mango tree by the field, Adoley and her classmates sit resting on the grass with a hand over her calm chest.

pages.text: “Running, skipping, and active games help your heart and muscles grow strong,” said Mr Kotei. “School-age children need about an hour of active play every day, and plenty of clean water to drink.”
sentences: “Running, skipping, and active games help your heart and muscles grow strong,” said Mr Kotei.
“School-age children need about an hour of active play every day, and plenty of clean water to drink.”
pages.alt: Cheerful schoolyard scene where pupils skip with ropes, pass a football, and drink clean water from reusable bottles.

pages.text: “However, if you ever feel dizzy, have pain in your chest, or struggle to breathe, stop right away and tell a grown-up,” Mr Kotei added. Adoley nodded. She decided to skip with her rope for ten minutes every evening.
sentences: “However, if you ever feel dizzy, have pain in your chest, or struggle to breathe, stop right away and tell a grown-up,” Mr Kotei added.
Adoley nodded.
She decided to skip with her rope for ten minutes every evening.
pages.alt: Adoley holding a colourful skipping rope and nodding attentively to Mr Kotei beside the school veranda.
